_comment: THE NUMBERS IN THIS FILE ARE CONSERVATIVE AND UNVALIDATED.
BRIEF.md deliberately fixes no rate ceiling, no threshold and no cooldown,
and CLAUDE.md rule 8 forbids inventing one and then treating it as decided.
Every value here exists so that a ceiling EXISTS and is enforced; none of
them has been checked against a real source's behaviour, because at this
phase this repository fetches no real source. Change them deliberately, in
a commit that says why, and never upwards against an anti-bot-protected
target without the owner (BRIEF.md constraint 7).
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored by the
loader. Every other key is required: the governor has no built-in default
and refuses to start on a file that is missing one.

http._comment: Per-request timeout, and the cap on how much of a response body enters this process.

_comment: One entry per hostname this system may contact, keyed by the lower-case
hostname without a port. A host with no entry here is REFUSED: there is
no default-permissive rate anywhere in the governor.
127.0.0.1 is the only host this repository contacts today - the test
harness's stub server and the local Postgres container are on it - and
loopback is owed no politeness, which is why its numbers are loose.
SOURCE-3 adds the first real host together with the ceiling that source's
own published terms and BRIEF.md constraint 4 justify.
productToken is what a robots.txt user-agent line is matched against,
case-insensitively (RFC 9309 2.2.1).
cacheBoundMs may not exceed 86400000: RFC 9309 2.4 says a crawler SHOULD
NOT use a cached robots.txt for more than 24 hours. Six hours is chosen
below the ceiling so a host that ADDS a disallow rule is obeyed sooner;
one extra robots request per host per six hours is not a politeness cost.
parsingLimitBytes may not fall below 512000: RFC 9309 2.5 says the
parsing limit MUST be at least 500 kibibytes.
How long a host is held after a 429 that carries no Retry-After, and
after a Retry-After this system could not read or that named an instant
already past. A host that says 'too many requests' and nothing else is
asking for a lot less traffic, so this is deliberately long.
The default per-source breaker. A source may override it under
sources.<id>.breaker. failureRateThreshold is the error-or-block rate,
in (0, 1], at which the source is paused; minimumOutcomes is how many
outcomes must be inside the window before that rate means anything.
One entry per adapter that may ask the governor for anything. A source
that is not listed here is REFUSED, because its breaker settings and its
allowance would otherwise be unknown.
A METERED source adds an allowance block:
"allowance": { "limit": <requests per period>, "periodMs": <period>,
"warnFraction": <0..1> }
and the limit comes from THAT source's own published terms. No such
number is written here: this phase fetches no real source, and SOURCE-3
is where the sanctioned API's published allowance is read and adopted.
The two source ids below are the ones packages/shared already names on
the observation context.
